strongest_angle: An in-depth analysis comparing the published feats, detection limits, and canonical abilities of Arthur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes and Maurice Leblanc's Arsene Lupin, explicitly labelled as analysis.

key_facts.fact: In June of 1906, Maurice Leblanc published Sherlock Holmes Arrive Trop Tard featuring the character Herlock Sholmès as a rival to Arsene Lupin.
Arthur Conan Doyle published the first Sherlock Holmes story A Study in Scarlet in 1887, following Edgar Allan Poe's 1841 invention of the detective story.
Sherlock Holmes is described in canonical comparisons as a consulting detective residing in London and Sussex, whereas Arsene Lupin is a gentleman burglar based in Paris.
